slides.texte_overlay:
Classic skills that make you
the man nobody forgets
Knowing how to carve and serve. A roast chicken at a family dinner, cut cleanly and served to everyone first. It's an old skill, and people notice the man who does it.
Dancing a simple slow dance. At a wedding, with your grandmother, your partner, a friend. Knowing a few basic steps makes the moment special for both of you.
Telling a story at a dinner table. A short, funny, well-timed story. Grandfathers were masters at it, and the man who can do it today is remembered at every party.
Knowing a bit of history. I do five minutes a day of history, art or science, and old-fashioned general knowledge still impresses people more than any gadget.
slides.texte_sophia: I do five minutes a day on a micro-learning app like the Sophia app. History, art, science. Old-fashioned general knowledge still impresses more than any gadget.

slides.texte_overlay: Shining your own shoes. A tin of polish, a brush, ten minutes on a Sunday. Well-kept shoes are a classic sign of a man who takes care of the details.
Lighting a proper fire. At a cabin, a beach, a garden. Building a fire from scratch is a primal skill, and everyone gathers around the man who can do it.
Writing a heartfelt speech. A best man speech, a retirement toast, a few words at a funeral. Finding the right words for big moments is a gift people never forget.
